items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: Eddie Atkins playing trombone. Lorenzo To playing clarinet.

ctx.x: And I played out there with him. And he had Manuel Perez played trumpet. Eddie Atkins playing trombone. Lorenzo To playing clarinet.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1958-08-08; 1958-09-03
items.q: And we all played up there, Madison Palina, at the Sonia with myself, Emmanuel Perez, Teo, Lorenzo Teo, Cantrell, Frank Aime

ctx.x: And that first job done in the Chicago, the Chinese restroom, is that on sort of the west side?

I was over on the west side, yeah. I was over on, I think I was over on Madison. I was over on Madison, some left in there, Palina, Madison Palina. And we all played up there, Madison Palina, at the Sonia with myself, Emmanuel Perez, Teo, Lorenzo Teo, Cantrell, Frank Aime, and Dixieland, and the only Dixieland band was the other. The original five. There was in one corner and there was the other corner.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: Eddie Atkins on trombone. Mm-hmm. Lorenzo Teal on clarinet.

ctx.x: I had a band. I had a band. Manuel Perez on trumpet. Mm-hmm. Eddie Atkins on trombone. Mm-hmm. Lorenzo Teal on clarinet.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: Lorenzo Teo, you see. Was playing clarinet. I played bass.

ctx.x: Lorenzo Teo, you see. Was playing clarinet. I played bass. Then the Dixon Land, the original Dixon Land, uh, jazz band from New Orleans, white boys, Dixon Land 5, we played on Madison and Paulina on the west side, the Osonia. They in one corner was another corner.
Oh, yeah? You mean the same place? In the same place.
